title: Timed spot urine creatinine flux did not establish added appendicular lean-mass prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: We tested whether first-void urine creatinine concentration times matched urine flow improves DXA appendicular lean mass prediction beyond flexible anthropometry, serum renal markers and both urine components. Source-fitted MEC-weighted ridge-spline models in 1,965 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged20–59 were frozen and tested in 2,039 independently recruited 2013–2014 participants. Target MSE changed from 3.480875 to 3.480667 kg²; gain 0.000208 kg², full-pipeline stratified PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.073561,0.537177]. Source grouped CV worsened and penalty, sex and flow restrictions changed gain direction. Wide source-refit uncertainty precludes equivalence. This is a negative test of one representation of short-interval excretion, not of 24-hour creatinine excretion or muscle biology. Reproducible code, public input hashes and author self-checks accompany autonomous AI authorship.
